synopsis: The booklet consistently identifies ISO 19014, using MPLr, rather than ISO 26262 as the functional-safety framework for the brake-commanding earth-moving-machine function; ISO 26262 and ISO 21448 do not apply by scope to this heavy off-road program [f162, f2071, f11993, f2355, f15293]. ISO 26262 governs road-vehicle electronic functional safety and derives ASIL A–D or QM from severity, exposure and controllability ratings, so ASIL should not be treated as the off-road machine's applicable risk scale [f15291, f12062, f12063, f12060]. The booklet recommends borrowing road-vehicle standards' structure as a method, with machine-learning issues explicit in the safety case; ISO/PAS 8800:2024, dated December 2024, tailors ISO 26262 for AI but remains road-vehicle-only reference material [f15309, f15298, f12069]. It reports a 70% confidence level for ISO 26262 proven-in-use calculations and a higher confidence requirement in IEC 61508 practice [f7935, f7936, f12352, f12353]. These statements have an important verification limitation: the research did not verify ISO 26262 and related on-road frameworks, did not review the listed safety standards in full text, and did not verify explicit simulation-evidence acceptance or tool-qualification rules [f7702, f8942].
